label: a missing build stamp reads as FRESH instead of stale, so a row that never got a stamp is permanently unpublishable with no error to see
find:
if stamp is None:
        return True
replace:
if stamp is None:
        return False

label: the staleness window becomes a constant again, so a healthy long build gets a second sandbox enqueued on top of it
a non-positive timeout yields a zero window, so every in-flight build reads as stale and the guard stops guarding
queued stops counting as in-flight, so a publish waiting behind the cap enqueues a second build and spends twice
a terminal 'failed' status blocks a new build, so one bad build wedges the site until someone edits the database
find:
if status not in IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES:
        return True
replace:
if status in TERMINAL_STATUSES and status != "failed":
        return True

label: a naive datetime is rejected as unreadable, so every row from an older writer looks stale and the guard silently stops blocking
find:
if value.tzinfo is None:
        return value.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
replace:
if value.tzinfo is None:
        return None

label: is_in_flight is aliased to the spend decision, so a stale row renders as idle to a viewer while a build may still be running
build_job_id becomes transient like DP0-4's, so a client that reloads during a queued build loses its polling handle
